blocks.content: The Richter scale measures the magnitude of an earthquake, while the Mercalli scale measures its intensity based on observed effects.

rows: I to XII (1 to 12, Roman numerals)
Human observation and structural damage reports

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Earthquake magnitude relates to the total energy released at the source and is measured quantitatively on the Richter scale.
Earthquake intensity measures the visible impact and destruction caused at a specific location using the Mercalli scale.
The Richter scale is logarithmic, meaning a unit increase represents a 10-fold increase in wave amplitude and approximately 32-fold increase in energy.
The hypocenter (focus) is the point of origin inside the Earth, whereas the epicenter lies directly above it on the surface.
Seismographs record seismic waves to determine the epicenter location and the depth of the focus.
Richter Scale measures Magnitude (energy released), whereas Mercalli Scale measures Intensity (damage observed).
An increase of 1 unit on the Richter scale corresponds to roughly 32 times more energy being released.
The point on the surface directly above the hypocenter is the epicenter, which typically experiences the strongest ground shaking.
